title: Embedding robustness sandbox and scalable canary runner
creator: Maya Singh
description: Build a reproducible evaluation harness that measures embedding accuracy and reranker effectiveness across quality, latency, and scale dimensions. The harness will support: curated reference corpora (golden queries + relevance tiers), offline metrics (nDCG, MRR, cosine calibration), latency-aware utility metrics, synthetic perturbation tests, and a horizontally scalable canary runner that executes nightly and on deploys.
motivation: Current embedding regressions are discovered too late and only via customer tickets or ad-hoc benchmarks. We need deterministic, versioned evaluations that combine quality signals with latency/throughput profiles so model and infra changes can be judged by production-relevant trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned golden corpus with 1K+ human-labeled queries spanning short/long contexts and cross-domain variations is stored in the evaluation bucket and referenced by harness
Nightly canary runs execute end-to-end against staging and produce a dashboard of quality and latency deltas vs baseline
Automated alerts trigger when core metrics (nDCG@10, median latency, 95th latency, cosine calibration error) regress beyond configurable thresholds
Canary runner horizontally scales to at least 200 concurrent eval workers without coordinator bottlenecks
Bench results are reproducible: same seed + dataset + model version -> identical metric outputs within tolerance
implementation_notes: Leverage existing embed eval tooling where possible but introduce a new lightweight coordinator service (stateless) that schedules tasks to worker pods
Workers will run synthetic perturbations (token-level noise, paraphrase substitutions, context truncation) to surface brittleness
Use a compact artifact manifest: dataset_id, model_id, seed, runtime_config. Store manifests in S3 and snapshot to release tags
Integrate with telemetry to record per-query latency distributions and KV cache hit rates so we can correlate quality vs cache effectiveness
Provide a permissive CLI for local reproducibility and a GitHub Action to run quick smoke checks on PRs changing ranking/model code
progress_updates: 2026-01-22: Kickoff meeting with PM, Dataset owner, and Reliability — scope refined to include latency-aware metrics
2026-01-30: Prototype coordinator pattern implemented (stateless job dispatcher) and tested with 10 workers
2026-02-12: Curated seed set (420 queries) assembled from support logs and internal product personas; annotators engaged for relevance tiers
2026-02-25: Baseline metrics collected for two model families (open-1.5, quant-1.5) across staging infra; noticed 15% degradation in nDCG for quantized variant on long queries
2026-03-04: Canary runner configured to post results to the new embeddings QA dashboard (dashboard link added to links)
2026-03-09: Load test: coordinator sustained 220 workers for 30 minutes; discovered AWS API throttling—mitigation plan in decisions
decisions: Coordinator will be stateless; state tracked in S3 manifests and DynamoDB job index to avoid single-node failures
Alert thresholds: nDCG@10 drop >3% or median latency increase >20% triggers P0 smoke; smaller deltas create triage tickets
Use cosine distance calibration and add a small calibration dataset for per-model thresholding rather than global thresholds
Synthetic perturbations included as first-class tests — these run in parallel to human-labeled goldens to catch regressions that human sets miss
risks: Annotation bottleneck: human labeling for a broad cross-domain corpus may delay finalization — mitigation: staged rollouts and synthetic augmentation
False positives from synthetic perturbation tests could create alert fatigue — mitigation: combine signals and require consensus for P0
S3/DynamoDB consistency edge cases could cause worker double-processing — mitigation: idempotent workers and job leasing semantics
test_plan: Unit tests for coordinator and worker; CI must run CLI smoke harness on every PR touching ranking code
Integration test: full canary run in a sandbox project, verify metrics match local reproducible run
Chaos test: simulate worker pod termination during long-run to ensure job leases reassign correctly
Performance test: measure end-to-end canary throughput and coordinator latency under 500 simulated workers
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): land coordinator + worker + small golden set, run nightly in staging for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (expanded): add full curated corpus and synthetic perturbations; enable dashboard alerts and notify SRE
Phase 3 (GA): enable canary for model deploys and add PR gate that runs a 5-min smoke canary for model changes
